messages.body_plain:
The question is relevant indeed!

It's exactly what I want to do. I created two web processes of which  
one is an optional successor of the other. If the second process is  
executed, it needs one R-object of the first process.

There is a Tomcat machine and a Rserve machine running and for  
different reasons I don't want to save the R-object on the Rserve  
machine but in the webapps directory of the Tomcat.

Therefore the question is again: What is the best way to transfer R- 
objects from Rserve to JRClient and back to Rserve?


Christian



> Hi Simon and others,
>
> The question below is no longer relevant, as the user in question  
> has got write access for Rserve on the one machine to the webapps  
> directory of the Tomcat installation on the other machine.
>
> Best regards,
>
> Cor
>
> C. J. Lieftink MSc, MA | The Netherlands Cancer Institute |  
> Division of Molecular Carcinogenesis | researchgroup Beijersbergen  
> | Room B.7.040 | Plesmanlaan 121 | 1066 CX | Amsterdam | The  
> Netherlands |  phone: 0031 20 512 7865 fax: 0031 20 512 1954 |  
> email: c.lieftink at nki.nl | http://www.nki.nl
>
>
>
>> -----Original Message-----
>> From: Cor Lieftink
>> Sent: Fri 9/5/2008 9:43
>> To: stats-rosuda-devel at listserv.uni-augsburg.de
>> Subject: Best way to transfer files generated in Rserve server to  
>> Java client.
>>
>> Hi Simon, and others,
>>
>> As you probably remember, we (NKI, HMS and IMCB) are using Rserve  
>> to run Rpackages from a Java web application called Screensaver.  
>> One of the users will run Rserver on a seperate machine as Tomcat.  
>> The Rpackage in question , cellHTS2, will generate a report on the  
>> filesystem with different html pages and images. However, these  
>> files have to be stored in a subdirectory of the Tomcat  
>> installation directory, that is on the other machine. Can you  
>> advise us the best way to transfer the data within the same  
>> connection from the Rserve server to the Java client, in  this  
>> case the Tomcat machine?  A solution suggested by IMCB is to use  
>> the  Rserve class RFileInputStream which transfers files from  
>> Rserve server to the client. However it seems to transfer one file  
>> at a time. Zipping would be probably an answer, although it is not  
>> clear to us how you can do that from Rserve and/or R.
>>
>> Thanks for your reply in advance!
>>
>> Cor

>> C. J. Lieftink MSc, MA | The Netherlands Cancer Institute |  
>> Division of Molecular Carcinogenesis | researchgroup Beijersbergen  
>> | Room B.7.040 | Plesmanlaan 121 | 1066 CX | Amsterdam | The

messages.body_plain:
Hi and thanks for the rJava package.

Since today there occured problems installing rJava on two Linux 
machines (Ubuntu 8.10 and Debian etch), I want to give two remarks.

The install.packages("rJava") call stopped with:

checking JNI data types... configure: error: One or more JNI types
differ from the corresponding native type. You may need to use
non-standard compiler flags or a different compiler in order to fix
this.
ERROR: configuration failed for package 'rJava'

Taking a look at the test program 

#include <jni.h>
int main(void) {
  return (sizeof(int)==sizeof(jint) && sizeof(long)==sizeof(long) &&
sizeof(jbyte)==sizeof(char) && sizeof(jshort)==sizeof(short) &&
sizeof(jfloat)==sizeof(float) && sizeof(jdouble)==sizeof(double))?0:1;
}

I noticed that the problem was that libjvm.so was not found. After 
adding the correct directory to LD_LIBRARY_PATH or LD_RUN_PATH, rJava 
could be installed. So, could the error message perhaps consider that
the program failed out of another reason?

Also the tautology "sizeof(long)==sizeof(long)" appears strange to me. 
Is this really what you want?

Best regards, Kornelius.

seems I am not getting anywhere any more. I Thus I would be EXTREMELY

Ciao,
thanks a lot

Michaela

messages.body_plain:
On Oct 24, 2008, at 10:23 AM, David Swartz wrote:

> I am using JGR on Mac OS X 10.5. How can I increase the JVM heap  
> size? The default is 512Mb which is too low for some tasks.
>

Essentially you have to change the setting in main.c line 43 of the  
launcher:

static char *xmx = "-Xmx512m"; /* default memory setting */

and re-build the launcher.

Step by step (in Terminal) - you'll need Xcode installed:

curl -s http://www.rforge.net/JGR/snapshot/JGR_1.6-2.tar.gz | \
tar fvxz -
cd JGR/launcher/macosx
open main.c
# edit the line 43 to whatever you desire and save it
xcodebuild
# the JGR.app should be in the build/Default directory
# see the second-to-last line of the output

Cheers,
Simon

On Oct 15, 2008, at 9:26 AM, Kornelius Rohmeyer wrote:

> Hi and thanks for the rJava package.
>
> Since today there occured problems installing rJava on two Linux
> machines (Ubuntu 8.10 and Debian etch), I want to give two remarks.
>
> The install.packages("rJava") call stopped with:
>
> checking JNI data types... configure: error: One or more JNI types
> differ from the corresponding native type. You may need to use
> non-standard compiler flags or a different compiler in order to fix
> this.
> ERROR: configuration failed for package 'rJava'
>
> Taking a look at the test program
>
> #include <jni.h>
> int main(void) {
>  return (sizeof(int)==sizeof(jint) && sizeof(long)==sizeof(long) &&
> sizeof(jbyte)==sizeof(char) && sizeof(jshort)==sizeof(short) &&
> sizeof(jfloat)==sizeof(float) && sizeof(jdouble)==sizeof(double))?0:1;
> }
>
> I noticed that the problem was that libjvm.so was not found. After
> adding the correct directory to LD_LIBRARY_PATH or LD_RUN_PATH, rJava
> could be installed. So, could the error message perhaps consider that
> the program failed out of another reason?
>

Can you send me your config.log, please? This should not fail for that  
reason, because there is another preceding test that checks whether  
JNI works at all. Checking the types is performed only after the JNI  
test was successful, so your conclusion doesn't sound right.
Also please make sure you have configured R correctly with Java  
support (sudo R CMD javareconf), because that is there LD_LIBRARY_PATH  
is set - your should not be setting it manually.


> Also the tautology "sizeof(long)==sizeof(long)" appears strange to me.
> Is this really what you want?
>

Yes, because jlong and long don't always match due to the way it's  
defined in Java. The test should produce no code, but it just reminds  
me of that issue ;).

Cheers,
Simon

messages.body_plain:
Michaela,

I have replicated your setup and cannot reproduce the problem (except  
that I'm using R 2.8.0 but I didn't see anyone complain with R 2.7.2  
either). JRI works just fine for me.

Have you tried running the examples in $R_HOME/library/rJava/jri?
All you need is something like:
cd C:\Program Files\R\R-2.8.0\library\rJava\jri
set PATH=%PATH%;C:\Program Files\R\R-2.8.0\bin
java -cp JRI.jar;examples rtest

It works in the setup described above. I would strongly suggest you  
don't set anything else unless you really know what you're doing.

If in doubt, try running JGR - it sets everything up correctly.

Cheers,
Simon

On 10/25/08 11:00 AM, "Simon Urbanek" <simon.urbanek at r-project.org> wrote:

> 
> On Oct 24, 2008, at 10:23 AM, David Swartz wrote:
> 
>> I am using JGR on Mac OS X 10.5. How can I increase the JVM heap
>> size? The default is 512Mb which is too low for some tasks.
>> 
> 
> Essentially you have to change the setting in main.c line 43 of the
> launcher:
> 
> static char *xmx = "-Xmx512m"; /* default memory setting */
> 
> and re-build the launcher.
> 
> Step by step (in Terminal) - you'll need Xcode installed:
> 
> curl -s http://www.rforge.net/JGR/snapshot/JGR_1.6-2.tar.gz | \
> tar fvxz -
> cd JGR/launcher/macosx
> open main.c
> # edit the line 43 to whatever you desire and save it
> xcodebuild
> # the JGR.app should be in the build/Default directory
> # see the second-to-last line of the output
> 
> Cheers,
> Simon
> 
>

> The constructor does not take any arguments.  So I need to set the  
> fields
> after I create the object.  Is there a simple way to do this  
> directly from
> R?  I could create a java method setOrder that will set all  
> parameters,
> but if I can do it from R, why not.
>
> I don't know how to do this.  For example I would like to set the  
> field
> "m_auction" to "BUY".  I tried
>>    ref$m_action <- "BUY"
>>    .jfield(ref, , "m_action")
> Error in .jfield(ref, , "m_action") : cannot find class BUY
>>
>
> If you can point me in the right direction, it will be great.

?.jfield

.jfield(ref, "m_action") <- "BUY"
.jfield(ref, "m_auxPrice") <- 10.50

However, with double/int be careful since your replacement value must  
be of the correct type (in order to find the right field by type), so  
for example
.jfield(ref, "m_auxPrice") <- 10L # do not do that!
will not work because 10L is an integer and the field is double, you  
have to use
.jfield(ref, "m_auxPrice") <- as.double(x)
if x can potentially be an integer. The same applies vice-versa, e.g.
.jfield(ref, "m_orderId") <- as.integer(x)

Cheers,
Simon
